editorial: When the dust settles on a quiet brick wall, you feel the weight of a life left behind and the promise of justice you never expected. A Working Man fuses the grit of a construction site with the cold precision of a former operative, turning the city’s underbelly into a relentless battlefield. Arlo Hartmann’s bare‑spoken performance drives the entire narrative, evoking raw desperation in almost every frame. A minor pacing lag in the mid‑section slows the otherwise swift escalation, but it barely distances the audience. You will find this in‑your‑soul unease particularly compelling if you are a fan of psychological thrillers steeped in moral ambiguity.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
